Company filings are kept here under their own headings (sections 3 and 4) and are marked as filings; they are not government documents. The project's owner, Nov 23, 2026 (04:01 UTC), asked whether they should stay here or move to Tier 2: "keep them."

Written Nov 20, 2026 (UTC), after the project owner's question: "are we leaning too heavily on reporting. what about government documents themselves." First written as a local note; now part of the project's public copy.

**Revised later on Nov 20, 2026** after three additions: (1) every one of the 103 lines of the policies list was read against its saved page (97 confirmed, 5 confirmed in part, 1 page unreadable; all 207 quotations found again by script); (2) the Internet Archive was asked for the pages not held; (3) the Commerce Secretary's Senate testimony of Apr 22, 2026 was found and saved. The items of that reading that bear on the argument are folded in below.

**Revised Nov 23, 2026** after the second search (five searches run side by side, 1,216 rows) and about thirty follow-up searches. Added: Nvidia's own wording on China filing by filing; the other chip makers' filings; Chinese companies' annual reports and results calls; the House Foreign Affairs Committee's table of licence applications by status; US reports that read Beijing's acts as leverage; published commentary in state and Party media (new section 2.6); seven more provincial plans, local voucher rules and tenders; the evaluation centre's own lists; official trade statistics. Every quotation added was found by script in the saved copy.

**Rule for this file.** Six kinds of source are used as evidence: (A) texts issued by the Chinese party-state; (B) public statements by named Chinese officials on official sites; (C) United States government documents and officials' recorded words; (D) company filings and published statements; (E) published commentary in state and Party media, and published statements of industry bodies (section 2.6), which are not orders; (F) named people's words on the record as carried by a transcript or a press report, marked as such. Machine captions of a broadcast are marked «machine captions, not checked by ear». Press reports that cite unnamed people appear only in section 6, as the second tier; a press report of a named person's words on the record is kind (F) and is marked as such. Every quotation was read in the saved copy (the id in square brackets names it). English renderings of Chinese are the project's own and are not official translations.

**How much of the first assessment was reporting.** Of the 55 sources the first assessment cites, 19 are official texts or statements, 4 are company filings or statements, 20 are news reports, and the rest analysis and other. So about four in ten of its sources were press.

## 1. What the documents establish, in six sentences

1. Since 2016 the Party's leader has said in published speeches that core technology controlled by others is the greatest hidden danger and that home-made products "must be used"; in 2025 the Central Committee wrote "extraordinary measures" for integrated circuits into the five-year plan.
2. That line is in binding and planning documents: Party and government organs at township level and above, the public institutions directly under Party committees and governments at those levels, and the departments' public institutions that provide support to those organs, must when buying desktop and portable computers and general-purpose servers require that the CPU and the operating system pass the security-and-reliability evaluation (joint notices of the finance and industry ministries), and the published lists of processors (2023) and of AI chips (2026) that passed name only entities registered in China (applying is voluntary and open only to such entities); where products made in China and other products compete in one government purchase, those made in China get a 20% price preference in the evaluation; provinces and cities set targets for the share of home-made chips in new computing centres (Jiangsu 70% or more by 2030 and 50% by 2025, both marked indicative; Sichuan aims for over 50% and Guangdong for 70%; Shanghai over 50% by 2025 and over 70% independently controllable; Tianjin over 60% by 2026; Hebei 60% or more of software and hardware; Inner Mongolia 50% or more; Shandong 90% in a newspaper's account). Two limits, both in the documents: every binding purchase rule read is addressed to state bodies or to public money, and in each of the three purchase notices the same sentence adds that other units may leave this requirement out; and every home-made percentage found is provincial or municipal, none national.
3. Regulators acted against Nvidia by name: the market regulator announced on Dec 9, 2024 that it had recently opened an antitrust case and the cyberspace regulator summoned the company over the H20 (Jul 31, 2025).
4. Official Chinese documents also show what the companies used and wanted: a Shanghai government reply says that among the city's computing suppliers internet companies' own clusters run mainly on Nvidia cards while the three big operators mainly buy Huawei's and other home-made intelligent-computing clusters; an official of the state planner's policy research office said at its press conference that it is guiding home-made large models to do more to adapt to home-made chips; a Party-journal investigation says migration is costly and slow.
5. Two companies say in filings that the state stopped purchases: Nvidia ("restricted by the PRC government") and Alibaba ("requested Chinese technology companies to halt purchases of certain chips"). The US Commerce Secretary told the Senate the same on Apr 22, 2026, as his "understanding": the cloud companies "want to buy these chips" and the "Chinese central government has not let them as of yet".
6. The same body of documents holds the other side: every leadership text keeps an "open door" clause; ministers welcomed Nvidia by name; the commerce ministry attacks US controls and smooths the way for Chinese companies' computing centres abroad; local vouchers pay for rented computing that is not home-made too (of 93 rules found by searches that went province by province and city by city, saved and read and counted, not a census of every local government, 81 state no higher rate for home-made computing, 80 of them at one rate for all and one, Hangzhou's, at two rates by a type of computing facility it does not name, and 8 pay other computing at a lower rate; 4, Sichuan's, Ningbo's, Huangyan district's and the Changsha zone's, pay for home-made computing only; and 9 of the 81 also give home-made computing money to build, buy or run its facilities, an award for adapting to it, or a condition on suppliers, by another provision of the same rule: a premium beside a payment that stays open to other computing); two universities publish notices of Nvidia hardware, holding suppliers to the government procurement law's conditions; the 20% preference goes by where a product is made, with foreign-funded firms treated equally; and Baidu and Alibaba tell investors that their own chips are in use or in scaled production. And US government documents read parts of Beijing's conduct, antitrust investigations among them, as leverage or retaliation in trade talks, while the Trade Representative calls the purchase decision China's own (section 4).

**What follows.** On documents alone, the claim "the state's declared policy pulled against what its AI companies were using and buying" is established. The claim "Beijing forbade the purchases" is established only through the two company filings and the US officials in section 4; Beijing itself has published no such instruction and its spokesmen decline to confirm one (section 5).

## 2. Chinese party-state documents: the push toward home-made chips

### 2.1 The leadership line

- Xi Jinping, forum on cybersecurity and informatization, Apr 19, 2016: "核心技术受制于人是我们最大的隐患" (core technology being controlled by others is our greatest hidden danger); and of home-made products, "该用的就要用" (what should be used must be used) [cn-xi-20160419]. The same speech speaks of internet companies by kind: "一个互联网企业即便规模再大、市值再高,如果核心元器件严重依赖外国,供应链的“命门”掌握在别人手里,那就好比在别人的墙基上砌房子,再大再漂亮也可能经不起风雨,甚至会不堪一击。" (however large an internet company and however high its market value, if it depends heavily on foreign countries for core components and the "vital gate" of its supply chain is in others' hands, it is like building a house on someone else's foundation: however big and handsome, it may not stand wind and rain, and may fall at a single blow) [cn-policy-xi-coretech-2016]. This is the closest published statement by Xi to the position of the AI companies and Nvidia. It is not an order, and the same speech has the open-innovation passage (section 5). The "must be used" phrase stands in a passage that accepts first flaws: "我们自己推出的新技术新产品,在应用中出现一些问题是自然的。可以在用的过程中继续改进,不断提高质量。如果大家都不用,就是报一个课题完成报告,然后束之高阁,那永远发展不起来。" (it is natural that new technologies and products we bring out ourselves show some problems in use; they can go on being improved as they are used and their quality steadily raised; if nobody uses them, all that comes of it is a project completion report filed and then put away on a high shelf, and they will never develop) [cn-policy-xi-coretech-2016].
- Xi Jinping at an integrated-circuit maker in Wuhan, Apr 2018 (Xinhua's report of Apr 28, 2018, held from People's Daily Online's database of his speeches [cn-ga03-jhsjk-xi-hubei-20180428] and from the Party members' site): "装备制造业的芯片,相当于人的心脏。心脏不强,体量再大也不算强。要加快在芯片技术上实现重大突破" (chips are to equipment manufacturing what the heart is to a person; if the heart is not strong, no size makes one strong; speed up major breakthroughs in chip technology) [cn-xi-breadth-1-relay1].
- Xi Jinping, Politburo study session on AI, Apr 25, 2025: "集中力量攻克高端芯片、基础软件等核心技术" (concentrate forces to conquer core technologies such as high-end chips and basic software) [cn-xi-round-j-6].
- Central Committee, recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, adopted Oct 23, 2025: "完善新型举国体制,采取超常规措施,全链条推动集成电路、工业母机、高端仪器、基础软件、先进材料、生物制造等重点领域关键核心技术攻关取得决定性突破" (improve the new whole-nation system, take extraordinary measures, and push along the whole chain for decisive breakthroughs in key core technologies in priority fields such as integrated circuits, machine tools, high-end instruments, basic software, advanced materials and biomanufacturing) [cn-policy-15fyp-recommendations]. The plan outline of March 2026 has the sentence from "采取超常规措施" onward (its opening words differ) and ties research to use: "强化以用促攻、攻用结合" (strengthen "use driving the tackling of key problems, tackling joined with use") [cn-policy-15fyp-outline].
- State Council, "AI Plus" opinions, Aug 2025: "支持人工智能芯片攻坚创新与使能软件生态培育" (support breakthrough innovation in AI chips and the growth of the enabling software ecosystem) [cn-policy-ai-plus].
- Eight bodies, "AI Plus Manufacturing" opinions, signed Dec 25, 2025 by the industry ministry, the cyberspace regulator, the state planner, the education and commerce ministries, the state-assets regulator, the market regulator and the data administration: "支持突破高端训练芯片、端侧推理芯片、人工智能服务器、高速互联、智算云操作系统等关键技术" (support breakthroughs in key technologies such as high-end training chips, on-device inference chips, AI servers, high-speed interconnect and intelligent-computing cloud operating systems); aim: "到2027年,我国人工智能关键核心技术实现安全可靠供给" (by 2027 China's key core AI technologies are in secure and reliable supply) [cn-policy-ai-manufacturing-279-wayback, a provincial department's copy in an Internet Archive capture of Jan 14, 2026]. No rule on buying foreign chips; the same document welcomes foreign capital (section 5).
- Cyberspace regulator, action plan for internet and information companies, Aug 21, 2026: "支持企业加强人工智能关键技术研究,研发高端人工智能芯片,突破高性能训练集群关键技术" (support companies in strengthening research on key AI technologies, developing high-end AI chips, and breaking through key technologies of high-performance training clusters) [cn-policy-cac-enterprise-plan-2026]. The regulator that the reporting names as restricting purchases here says it supports companies in developing high-end AI chips. It says nothing on which chips they may buy: the words 国产, 自主可控 and 安全可控 are not in the page (0 places each; "人工智能芯片" is found once, so the search could see a hit).
- State Council, AI development plan, 2017: "突破图形处理器等核心硬件" (make breakthroughs in core hardware such as graphics processors) [cn-policy-ai-plan-2017]. Graphics processors were named eight years before the Nvidia dispute.
- Xi Jinping, New Year address for 2026: "芯片自主研发有了新突破" (independent research and development of chips made new breakthroughs) [cn-policy-xi-newyear-2026].
- **Jan 30 to Oct 2026 · Xi Jinping's words on self-reliance and on the computing network in the window** (two speeches as published and three People's Daily accounts of his words; no foreign firm named). Words: Politburo study of Jan 30, 2026, published May 31: "采取超常规措施，加大重点领域关键核心技术攻关力度，尽快解决制约未来产业发展的“卡脖子”问题" [cn-xi-round-f-3]; Feb 9, 2026, at the national park for information-technology innovation and application (国家信创园): "建设社会主义现代化强国，关键在科技自立自强，北京要发挥自身优势，在这方面作出更大贡献" [cn-le22-jhsjk-xi-beijing-20260209]; Jul 8, 2026: "综合运用财政、货币、科技、产业政策，促进自主研发技术产品推广应用和迭代升级" [cn-xi-science2026]; Sept 2026: "持续做大做强先进制造业，提升产业链自主可控水平" [cn-le22-jhsjk-xi-manufacturing-20260918], an instruction relayed at the national conference on advanced manufacturing, where the Premier said: "技术路线上更加注重高端自主" [cn-le22-jhsjk-xi-manufacturing-20260918]; Oct 2026: "实施“东数西算”工程、构建全国一体化算力网，是党中央一项重要部署" [cn-le22-jhsjk-xi-ulanqab-20261016]. Cuts: FOR on direction.
- **Apr 29 and May 2026 · Ding Xuexiang, vice premier** (a named official on the record). Self-reliance with an open clause: "我國人工智能隻有走自主創新發展之路，才有應對任何遏制打壓的底氣" [cn-factions-ding-both-lines-20260429]; "人工智能的發展，不能筑起封閉的圍牆，而應搭建互利合作的橋梁" [cn-factions-ding-both-lines-20260429]; "推动国产软硬件尽快从“可用”迈向“好用”" [cn-xi-ding-compute2026] (push home-made software and hardware from usable to good to use as soon as possible). - Earlier planning: Made in China 2025 (May 2015): "到2025年,70%的核心基础零部件、关键基础材料实现自主保障" (by 2025, 70% of core basic components and key basic materials to be self-supplied) [cn-policy-mic2025]. This clause is about components and materials in general, not chips alone. - **Sept 7, 2026 · Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, plan for the information and communications industry in the 15th five-year period** (a document, 工信部规〔2026〕188号; the ministry's own page and PDF, and three copies on other sites). - **Jan 18, 2024 and Apr 25, 2025 · The industry ministry and six other bodies on future industries; and Xi's Politburo study session, the passages beside the one the record holds** (a document; the leader's words in Xinhua's readout). The seven bodies' opinions on future industries ask for faster breakthroughs in GPU chips, low-latency cluster links and heterogeneous resource management, and for very large intelligent-computing centres. At the session where Xi called for conquering high-end chips (held), he also named government procurement among the policy tools for AI and called for broad international cooperation on AI. Neither text names a foreign firm or tells companies what to buy (英伟达 0 in both). Words: "发文字号: 工信部联科〔2024〕12号 成文日期: 2024-01-18" [cn-ga31-early2024-26]; "加快突破GPU芯片、集群低时延互连网络、异构资源管理等技术,建设超大规模智算中心" [cn-ga31-early2024-26]; "要综合运用知识产权、财政税收、政府采购、设施开放等政策" [cn-ga31-early2024-34]; "要广泛开展人工智能国际合作,帮助全球南方国家加强技术能力建设" [cn-ga31-early2024-34]. Cuts: FOR on direction (a published national aim, in January 2024, to speed breakthroughs in GPU chips), with an AGAINST clause (international cooperation).
- **Mar 5, 2026 (Xinhua's account of Mar 12, 2026) · Xi Jinping, with the Jiangsu delegation to the National People's Congress** (a published account of his words). After a deputy from Tongfu Microelectronics (通富微电子) spoke, he said: "中国的科技发展要在国际上开展合作的同时，坚持独立自主、自立自强，更好承担起我们的历史责任" [cn-ga31-counter-10] (China's technological development must, while cooperating internationally, hold to independence, self-reliance and self-strengthening, and better shoulder our historical responsibility). No chip, firm or purchase is named. Cuts: CONTEXT (both halves of the line in one sentence: cooperation abroad and self-reliance).
- **Dec 2025 · Xi Jinping at the Central Economic Work Conference, as People's Daily reports him (Dec 14, 2025, its own e-paper)** (the leader's words, in a report by the paper's reporters). Speaking of fitting policy to local conditions (因地制宜), he faulted places that take up chips because others do: "一些地方不顾实际，盲目追风口。看别人搞芯片，自己也搞。" [cn-ga31-xi2025-27] (some places ignore their real conditions and blindly chase the trend: seeing others go into chips, they go into chips too). Cuts: CONTEXT (the leader warns against local chip projects undertaken in imitation of others without regard to local conditions; the words are about localities getting into chips, not about which chips firms buy).

### 2.2 Purchasing rules that bind state bodies

- Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, notice on desktop computers, signed Dec 16, 2023: "乡镇以上党政机关,以及乡镇以上党委和政府直属事业单位及部门所属为机关提供支持保障的事业单位在采购台式计算机时,应当将CPU、操作系统符合安全可靠测评要求纳入采购需求" (Party and government organs at township level and above, the public institutions directly under Party committees and governments at those levels, and the departments' public institutions that provide support to those organs, shall when buying desktop computers include in the purchase requirement that the CPU and operating system meet the security-and-reliability evaluation) [cn-policy-desktop-2023]. The sentence ends "其他单位可不在采购需求中提出此项要求" (other units may leave this requirement out). The same clause, with the same ending, was published the same day (Dec 26, 2023; corrected Nov 23, 2026 from "issued that day": only the desktop notice's signing date was checked) for portable computers [cn-policy-laptop-procurement-2023] and for general-purpose servers [cn-policy-server-procurement-2023]. All three name the CPU and the operating system only; GPU and 人工智能 are not in any of the three pages (0 places; CPU is found in each). The server standard's annex, read since, words its row as key components «such as» the CPU and the operating system, has GPU 0 times, and has 人工智能 once, in an unstarred row on an optional AI computing unit of which no evaluation is asked (this section's entry on what «article 75» says). Four further standards of the same day, for workstations, all-in-one computers, operating systems and databases, end the same way (this section's row of Dec 16, 2023 on four further purchase standards).
- The evaluation list of Dec 26, 2023 names the processors that passed, in 18 numbered rows by a script's count of the saved table (some rows name more than one model), from HiSilicon, Loongson, the Wuxi institute (Sunway), Phytium, Hygon and Zhaoxin, the entities that submitted them (送测单位), each of which the trial guide then in force required to be registered in China [cn-ga31-evaluation-33]; the strings "Intel", "AMD" and "英特尔" are not in the copy (a provincial procurement site's PDF) [cn-policy-cpu-list-2023].
- **An evaluation list for AI chips now exists.** Announcement 2026 No. 2 of the same two evaluation centres, dated May 26, 2026, "附表一、人工智能训练推理芯片" (table 1, AI training and inference chips): Ascend 310 and 910 (HiSilicon), Zhenwu M530 and M890 (T-Head, "Alibaba’s chip design unit" in Alibaba's release of Sept 25, 2026, which calls the Zhenwu M890 the predecessor of T-Head's new chip [cn-ga31-twelve-35]), and one chip each from Biren, Hygon, Iluvatar CoreX, MetaX and Moore Threads; nine chips, seven makers, all registered in China, all level I, in that announcement [cn-policy-ai-chip-evaluation]. The centres' own pages are now saved: by the announcement of Sept 20, 2026, 11 AI chips from 8 makers have passed, all registered in China, among them "昇腾950 深圳市海思半导体有限公司 Ⅱ级" [cn-le14-itsec-2026-3]; applicants must be "中国境内注册的实体" [cn-le14-itsec-scope-20230727], and applying is voluntary, "由企业自愿向中国信息安全测评中心、国家保密科技测评中心" [cn-le14-itsec-scope-20230727]. Two limits remain: applying is voluntary, and no purchase rule read ties AI-chip buying to this list: the three 2023 notices name the CPU and the operating system only.
- The 2014 integrated-circuit outline already had a purchasing clause: "国家扩大内需的各项惠民工程和财政资金支持的重大信息化项目的政府采购部分,应当采购基于安全可靠软硬件的产品。鼓励基础电信和互联网企业采购基于安全可靠软硬件的整机和系统。" (the government-procurement part of the state's public-benefit projects to expand domestic demand and of major informatization projects supported by fiscal funds shall buy products based on secure and reliable software and hardware; basic telecom and internet companies are encouraged to buy complete machines and systems based on secure and reliable software and hardware) [cn-policy-2014-outline]. This is the earliest published text found that reaches internet companies' purchases; for them the word is "encouraged".
- Ministry of Finance, measures on government procurement of imported products, Dec 27, 2007: "第四条 政府采购应当采购本国产品,确需采购进口产品的,实行审核管理。" (article 4: government procurement shall procure domestic products; where imported products are really needed, review applies) [cn-policy-import-procurement-119]. For bodies spending public money, an imported product has needed the finance department's approval since 2007, save in projects involving national security and secrets, which the measures exclude (article 27), and for additions of the items already bought of up to 10% of the original contract's amount (articles 16 and 17); nothing here governs a company spending its own money.
- Cybersecurity Review Measures (in force Feb 15, 2022), among the factors a review weighs: "产品和服务的安全性、开放性、透明性、来源的多样性,供应渠道的可靠性以及因为政治、外交、贸易等因素导致供应中断的风险" (the security, openness, transparency and diversity of sources of the products and services, the reliability of supply channels, and the risk of supply being cut off for political, diplomatic, trade or other reasons) [cn-policy-review-measures]. On paper a chip under another country's export controls carries exactly that risk. No review of Nvidia products under these Measures was found in the pages read.
- Government Procurement Law, article 10: "政府采购应当采购本国货物、工程和服务" (government procurement shall procure domestic goods, works and services), with the exception, among others, of goods that "在中国境内无法获取或者无法以合理的商业条件获取" (cannot be obtained in China or cannot be obtained on reasonable commercial terms) [cn-policy-procurement-law-article10].
- Cybersecurity Law (as amended Oct 28, 2025), article 37: "关键信息基础设施的运营者采购网络产品和服务,可能影响国家安全的,应当通过国家网信部门会同国务院有关部门组织的国家安全审查" (operators of critical information infrastructure that purchase network products and services shall, where the purchase may affect national security, pass a national security review organised by the national cyberspace authority with the relevant departments of the State Council) [cn-policy-cyber-law-amended]. This is the legal footing of the Micron decision below.
- State Council General Office, notice of Sept 28, 2025 on home-made products in government purchasing, where home-made and other products compete in one purchase: "对本国产品的报价给予20%的价格扣除" (the bid price of home-made products is given a 20% deduction in evaluation) [cn-policy-domestic-product-standard-2025]. "Home-made" is defined by place of production, not by the maker's ownership: "产品应当在中国境内生产,即在中华人民共和国关境内实现从原材料、组件到产品的属性改变" (the product shall be produced in China, that is, the change of properties from raw materials and components into the product takes place within the customs territory of the People's Republic of China). The required shares of the cost of components produced in China are to be set, product by product, within five years of the notice taking effect; until a product's share requirement is in force, a product that meets that production test counts as home-made (the notice's equal-treatment clause is in section 5 below).
- **2023 to 2026 · The evaluation centres' own pages (China Information Technology Security Evaluation Center and the national secrecy evaluation centre)** (documents; the project before held only a trade site's copy of the May 2026 list). The security-and-reliability evaluation covers CPUs, AI training and inference chips, operating systems and databases; applicants must be entities registered in China; the rating weighs whether design, development and production were done in China; and applying is voluntary, with firms and users free to use the results or not. Words: "安全可靠测评主要面向计算机终端和服务器搭载的中央处理器（包括含人工智能加速单元的中央处理器）、人工智能训练推理芯片、操作系统、数据库" [cn-le14-itsec-scope-20230727]; "送测单位应为中国境内注册的实体" [cn-le14-itsec-scope-20230727] (applicants shall be entities registered in China); "设计、开发、生产等关键环节在中国境内完成的情况" [cn-le14-itsec-scope-20230727]; "由企业自愿向中国信息安全测评中心、国家保密科技测评中心（以下简称“测评机构”）申请产品检测，测评结果由企业和用户自主选择使用。" [cn-le14-itsec-scope-20230727] (firms apply of their own will ... firms and users choose for themselves whether to use the results); the guide is "安全可靠测评工作指南（V4.0）" [cn-le14-itsec-scope-20230727]. Nine announcements, Dec 26, 2023 to Sept 20, 2026, are saved; by a script's count 11 AI chips from 8 makers have passed, all registered in China as the guide requires of an applicant; the announcement of Sept 20, 2026 adds "昇腾950 深圳市海思半导体有限公司 Ⅱ级" [cn-le14-itsec-2026-3] and "昆仑芯M100 昆仑芯（北京）科技股份有限公司 I级" [cn-le14-itsec-2026-3]. Table: tables/chip_evaluations.tsv. Cuts: FOR, with the limit that applying is voluntary.
- **Dec 16, 2023 · Finance and industry ministries, four further purchase standards** (documents: workstations, all-in-one computers, operating systems, databases). Each binds the same state bodies and ends the same way; the workstation standard lists AI acceleration as a feature with no evaluation requirement on it. Words: "在采购工作站时，应当将CPU、操作系统符合安全可靠测评要求纳入采购需求，其他单位可不在采购需求中提出此项要求" [cn-le14-mof-workstation-standard-2023]; "在采购一体式计算机时，应当将CPU、操作系统符合安全可靠测评要求纳入采购需求，其他单位可不在采购需求中提出此项要求" [cn-le14-mof-allinone-standard-2023]; "支持 NPU/GPU 等 AI 加速模块" [cn-le14-mof-workstation-standard-2023-pdf]. Cuts: CONTEXT (narrow by their own words).
- **Jun 22, 2026 · Ministry of Finance, Caiku [2026] No. 10** (a document). Government buyers may not buy products made by 46 named American firms, not counting US-funded firms in China; the attached list gives the firms' names only, in Chinese and English, and 英伟达, NVIDIA, Intel, AMD, Micron, 美光, Qualcomm and 芯片 are each found 0 times in it (the control «Lockheed» 7 times). Words: "采购人在政府采购活动中，不得采购46家美国企业（不包括在华美资企业）生产的产品。" [cn-le14-mof-us-firms-measures-20260622]; "财库〔2026〕10号" [cn-le14-mof-us-firms-measures-20260622]; "Lockheed Martin" [cn-le14-mof-us-firms-list-20260622]. When Beijing published a by-name bar on American products for state buyers, none of the chip makers searched for above was on it. Cuts: CONTEXT (supports «guidance, not a published ban»).
- **Nov 7, 2024 and Jul 31, 2026 · Tenders of universities and of a state-funded firm that name home-made AI hardware** (documents: purchase notices). Fudan University sought equipment for a computing cluster, economy and high-performance home-made AI servers among it with storage, network and security equipment, under a ceiling of 54.73 million yuan for the whole; a state-funded firm in Qinghai sought one AI server to build a home-made computing node. Words: "经济型国产AI计算服务器（整机AI算力FP16≥2.2PFlops；FP32≥0.60PFlops）、高性能国产AI计算服务器" [cn-le17-ccgp-fudan-domestic-202411]; "最高限价（如有）：5473.000000 万元（人民币）" [cn-le17-ccgp-fudan-domestic-202411]; Tsinghua's "清华大学国产高性能 AI 服务器购置项目" [cn-o35-tsinghua-atlas-202409]; Sun Yat-sen's "中山大学国产智能计算系统采购项目" [cn-o35-ccgp-sysu-202412]. No tender found refuses Nvidia by name (see section 8). Cuts: FOR.
- **Nov 23 and 24, 2026 · Five buyers' notices on the national procurement site that name or require home-made computing** (documents: four notices in the site's central section, one in its local section; rows 45 to 49 of tables/procurement_records.tsv). The drug regulator's medical-device evaluation centre rented an eight-card home-made AI computing environment for a year and asked for its existing applications to be moved to a home-made AI computing architecture, the original not named (result, Nov 24); Peking University sought eight inference cards, imports not accepted, for work on home-made AI computing (tender, Nov 23); Central China Normal University bought one Huawei Atlas 800I A3 (award, Nov 24); the Institute of Modern Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences bought one DCU server, the DCU's maker not written (award, Nov 24); the First Affiliated Hospital of Guilin Medical University sought a platform with one home-made GPU machine (tender, Nov 24). Words: "完成现有应用从原人工智能计算架构向国产人工智能计算架构的适配迁移" [cn-ga13-ccgp-nmpa-cmde-ai-rental-27742397]; "基于国产AI算力开展模型推理验证和算法开发" [cn-ga13-ccgp-pku-inference-card-27734000]; "华为Atlas 800I A3" [cn-ga13-ccgp-ccnu-training-27739829]; "面向等离子体模拟计算DCU服务器" [cn-ga13-ccgp-cas-imp-dcu-27741809]; "国产GPU算力机1台" [cn-ga13-ccgp-df-guilin-med-ai-27746099]. Each is a notice of a tender or an award for one machine, a few cards or a year's rental, not a delivery; none names the maker of a chip (Huawei is named as the brand of a machine). Cuts: FOR.
- **Sept 27, 2024 and 2025 · «No imports» in two universities' notices sits beside Nvidia cards** (documents). The University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences sought to rent servers carrying eight Nvidia A800 or A100 cards under a notice that accepts no imported products or services; the Southern University of Science and Technology awarded the purchase of a server, its listed origin China, with eight Nvidia L40 cards under the line «refuse imports». Words: "本项目不接受进口" [cn-o35-ccgp-ucas-a100-202409]; "是否接受进口 拒绝进口" [cn-o35-sustech-00064]. So the procurement law's preference for domestic goods (section 2.2, the Government Procurement Law) sits, in these two notices, beside servers that hold Nvidia chips, the one bought with its origin listed as China (the project's reading of the two notices). Cuts: AGAINST a reading that state purchase rules shut out Nvidia chips.
- **Jun 19, 2025 · Fudan University, purchase intention for a home-made large-model training and inference server** (a document: the university's procurement centre, the page address dated Jun 19, 2025). One home-made large-model machine on an independently controllable hardware architecture, at least 3 PFlops a node; an intention, which the notice says is a preliminary plan. Words: "大模型国产训练推理服务器" [cn-ga31-early2024-43]; "拟采购拟采购一套国产高性能大模型一体机,该设备基于自主可控的硬件架构与国产化算法框架设计" [cn-ga31-early2024-43] (the page repeats 拟采购). Cuts: FOR.
- **Jun 30, 2026 · The evaluation centres' guide (V4.0), in its own words: who may apply, what is weighed, what stays unpublished** (a document; the China Information Technology Security Evaluation Center's own page, "2026-06-30 来源： 中国信息安全测评中心" [cn-le14-itsec-scope-20230727]; the words below stand in the saved page's body, not all in its text extract). Only an entity registered in China may apply, and it must meet eight conditions, among them that the product is on open sale or in use and that the applicant holds the product's full development documents, design materials, code and development environment; an applicant may submit at most two products of each kind in one intake period, and the kinds are CPUs (CPUs with AI acceleration units included), AI training and inference chips, operating systems, databases and printer controller chips. GPUs are not named as a kind; a GPU can pass as an AI training and inference chip (Biren's GPGPU passed in that kind: section 3.4, the row on two makers on the evaluation lists). The evaluation includes code review and a review of the development environment; a pass is valid for three years; a change in the applicant's actual controller or controlling stake while the pass is valid must be reported; and the applicant must keep unpublished matters of the evaluation confidential. The nine saved announcements of results list products with their applicants and grades, not who else applied or who failed. The guide's words 外资, 外商, 境外 and 国外 occur 0 times each (control: 中国境内 2), so it neither names foreign makers nor sets a minimum Chinese stake. The centre's application form offers the AI kind for desktops and servers: "人工智能训练推理芯片（□桌面 □服务器）" [cn-ga31-evaluation-30]. What a pass is for: the guide leaves its use to firms and users (section 2.2, the row on the centres' own pages); the state's purchase standards of 2023 require it for the CPU and operating system only. Cuts: CONTEXT (every maker on the lists is registered in China because no other may apply; whether a foreign maker's Chinese-registered unit ever applied cannot be known from the published pages).
- **Jul 2023 to May 2026 · When AI chips became a kind of the evaluation** (documents: the guide's earlier versions as other sites reproduce them, the centres' own pages for the lists). The trial guide, released on Jul 28, 2023 by the centre's account as a software-licensing service centre in Chongqing reproduces it (page of Jul 31, 2023), covers CPUs, operating systems and databases; the third version, as a security news site reproduces it (Jul 8, 2025), adds AI training and inference chips and printer controller chips; the fourth, of Jun 30, 2026, on the centre's own page, keeps them. - **Jun 18, Sept 9 and Nov 16, 2026 · Three buyers write the AI-chip evaluation into their purchase terms** (documents: two on the buyers' own sites, one as a payments news site reproduces it). The annex is headed "附件 通用服务器政府采购需求标准（2023 版）" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7] and prints no number, date or issuer of its own. It is one table of numbered rows (序号), not of articles: a tender document that cites its «第75条» (China Telecom's prequalification notice of Jul 5, 2024 does so for the CPU: section 3.6, [cn-ga31-operators-83]) means row 75. Row 75 (class 安全要求, indicator *关键部件安全要求, starred, not to be used as a scoring factor) reads, in its requirement cell, CPU 和操作系统等关键部件应当符合安全可靠测评要求 (key components such as the CPU and the operating system shall meet the security-and-reliability evaluation); the saved text breaks the cell over two lines, so it is checked in two parts: "CPU 和操作系统等关键部件应当符" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7] and "合安全可靠测评要求" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7]. Its use column tells the buyer where to look the results up: on the sites of the China Information Technology Security Evaluation Center and the national secrecy evaluation centre, named by government departments (broken over seven short lines in the server annex; the same cell stands less broken in the desktop annex: "通过政府有关部门指定的" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-9], "站查看安全可靠测评结果" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-9]). The row carries footnote 3, which says who must ask for it: "3)乡镇以上党政机关，以及党委和政府直属事业单位及部门所属为机关提供支持保障的事业单位在采购相关产品时，应当提出此项要求。" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7] (Party and government organs at township level and above, the public institutions directly under Party committees and governments and the departments' public institutions that provide support to the organs shall make this requirement when they buy the relevant products). What the star and the scoring column mean, from the annex's second page: "1)加“*”指标为必须纳入采购需求的指标，未加“*”的指标由采购人根据实际需要自行确定是否包含在采购需求中。" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7] (a starred indicator must go into the purchase requirement; an unstarred one the buyer includes or leaves out according to actual needs); "2)“是否可以作为评分因素”为“是”的指标，采购人可以根据实际需要在采购文件中设为评分项；为“否”的，不能设为评分项。" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7]. The row before it, 74, unstarred: "支持多集群作业管理功能" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7] (support for managing jobs across clusters). The row after it, 76, starred: "支持故障检测功能，可以检测到具" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7] (fault detection for parts such as memory and disks; the cell runs on). What the annex does not hold, by a script's count over its whole text: 国产 0, 自主可控 0, 本国 0, 进口 0, GPU 0, NPU 0, 智算 0, 智能计算 0, 英伟达 0, NVIDIA 0, and 华为, 海光, 飞腾, 龙芯 and 鲲鹏 each 0 (control: CPU 28 times, PCIe 18, 安全可靠测评 2). The word 等 (such as) leaves the list of key components open; the row names two. AI hardware is specified in row 43 alone (row 44, unstarred, names an AI computing unit only as the condition for offering a training-script migration tool), unstarred and with no evaluation asked of it: "若配备 AI 计算单元应符合如下要" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7], "a) 具备人工智能加速处理器，计算" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7] (if an AI computing unit is fitted, it shall have an AI accelerator processor, and so on); row 50, unstarred, lists an accelerator card among cards a buyer may ask for, "卡、显示功能卡、运算加速功能" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-7]. The six sibling standards of the same day carry the same row under other numbers, read in the saved annexes: desktop computers row 183 "CPU 和操作系统等关键部件应当符合" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-9], portable computers row 189 [cn-ga31-serverstd75-10], all-in-one computers row 179 [cn-ga31-serverstd75-11], workstations row 182 [cn-ga31-serverstd75-12]; operating systems rows 160 (desktop) and 165 (server), "操作系统应当符合安全可靠测评要求" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-13]; databases rows 105 (distributed) and 100 (centralized), "数据库应当符合安全可靠测评要求" [cn-ga31-serverstd75-15]. No explanation by either ministry of this row was found (a search of Nov 25, 2026 for the standard's title with 答记者问, 政策解读 and 起草说明 on the two ministries' sites; the same search returns the notice itself, the control). Cuts: CONTEXT (what a tender means by «article 75»: an evaluation condition on the processor and the operating system, which the notice makes binding on Party and government organs from the township level up, on the public institutions directly under Party committees and governments at those levels and on the departments' public institutions that provide support to the organs, and which other units may leave out, in the notice's words (a notice on government purchasing); the limit by origin lies in the evaluation, for which only entities registered in China may apply, as the rows on the evaluation centres' pages say; row 75 of the 2023 standard itself names no AI chip (row 43, which speaks of AI accelerators, asks no evaluation of them), so a buyer who asks the evaluation of an AI chip names a component that the row leaves unnamed).

### 2.3 Targets for computing centres

- Action plan for computing infrastructure, 工信部联通信〔2023〕180号, Oct 8, 2023, six bodies, the state-assets regulator among them (the ministry's own page: "工信部联通信〔2023〕180号" [cn-le27-miit-compute-infra-plan-2023]): "逐步形 成自主可控解决方案" (gradually form independently controllable solutions) and "鼓励算力基础设施采用安全可信的基础软硬件进行建设,保障供应链安全" (computing infrastructure is encouraged to be built with secure and trusted basic software and hardware, to safeguard supply-chain security) [cn-policy-compute-plan-pdf]. No share and no deadline.
- National computing-network opinions, Dec 25, 2023 (the state planner and four other bodies): "算力网关键核心技术基本实现安全可靠" (among the goals for the end of 2025: the key core technologies of the computing network to be in the main secure and reliable) [cn-policy-computing-network-1779]. No home-made share: 国产 and 自主可控 are not in the page (0 places each; "安全可靠" is found 4 times). **Every home-made percentage found so far is provincial or municipal; none is national.**
- Shanghai, "Computing Pujiang" plan for 2024 to 2025, of the city communications administration and ten other bodies ("上海市通信管理局等11个部门联合印发" [cn-ga31-early2024-49], a trade site's full copy; a government site of another province, the Shandong Big Data Bureau's, carries the plan with its issuing notice on a page dated 2024-04-01 [cn-ga31-unsaved3-plantexts6-http]; the issuer's own page not reached), as carried by Yicai, Mar 22, 2024: "到2025年,本市新建智算中心国产算力芯片使用占比超过50%,国产存储使用占比超过50%" (by 2025 home-made computing chips make up over 50% of use in the city's newly built intelligent computing centres, and home-made storage over 50%) [cn-policy-shanghai-domestic-target].
- Guizhou, provincial press conference as reported by People's Daily, Mar 24, 2026: "贵州算力总规模中,智算占比、国产化率、区域集中度均超过90%" (of Guizhou's total computing capacity, the share of intelligent computing, the home-made rate and the regional concentration are each above 90%) [cn-policy-guizhou-localization-2026]. The province's own figure; how the rate is counted is not given.
- Jiangsu, four-agency plan (苏通联〔2024〕7号, signed Apr 22, 2024 by the provincial communications administration, development and reform commission, industry department and data bureau with the provincial government's consent, posted Apr 25, 2024: "苏通联〔2024〕7号", "2024年4月22日" [cn-ga31-inth2-js-compute-plan-notice-2024]; the saved PDF, the notice's attachment, carries no date of its own): "新建算力中心国产算力芯片使用占比达 70%以上" [cn-factions-jiangsu-plan] (home-made computing chips to make up 70% or more of use in newly built computing centres). The plan's own table of indicators gives the row "新建算力中心国产算力芯片使用占比(%)" the values 50 for 2025 and 70 for 2030 and the label "预期性" (expected, that is, indicative); in that part of the table only the energy-efficiency row is labelled "约束性" (binding). So Jiangsu's 70% is a target for 2030, 50% is the target for 2025, and the plan itself marks both as indicative. (Corrected Nov 23, 2026: this line had said "Apr 2024" as if the page gave it, and left the years and the label to a search's account. A later reading noticed the missing date; the table in the PDF was then read.)
- Gansu, provincial government document 甘政发〔2026〕1号 of Jan 6, 2026, an "AI plus" action plan (hand-saved Nov 23, 2026; read whole): no share for home-made chips. It supports home-made computing in words: "支持国产化算力集群和全栈国产框架平台建设" (support the building of home-made computing clusters and full-stack home-made framework platforms) [man-cn-o39-gansu-ai-plus-2026]. Its two percentages are targets for 2027: about 70% for the spread of new-generation smart devices and agents, and more than 60% for the share of government services handled «intelligently» (智能办).
- Hunan (plan for green intelligent computing, 2025 to 2030, issued Feb 23, 2025) and Qinghai (two documents, of Feb 2024 and Aug 2026) were hand-saved on Nov 23, 2026 [man-cn-o39-hunan-green-compute-plan-2025] [man-cn-o39-qinghai-green-compute-2024] [man-cn-o39-qinghai-compute-15fyp-2026]. Their PDFs' text layers are damaged; the pages were read as images (transcriptions are kept beside the damaged copies, and the provinces' own HTML pages were read in Archive captures): none sets a share for home-made hardware. Hunan's table has nine goals, the PUE goal marked binding; Qinghai's 2026 table has seven indicators; Hunan's 95% is the present rate for chip-making equipment. Hunan's guiding opinion of Sept 30, 2024 (湘政办发〔2024〕34号), read whole on the provincial portal, sets no share either (this section's row of Sept 30, 2024).

- **Count of the 31 provincial-level governments, as of Nov 25, 2026.** 9 set a share for home-made computing, each by its plan's own measure: chips, equipment, hardware and software, or computing capacity (Jiangsu, Shanghai, Sichuan, Guangdong, Tianjin, Hebei, Inner Mongolia, Shandong, Zhejiang; Shandong's only in press accounts of a plan whose text is not held; Zhejiang's, found on Nov 25, 2026, is a project target for the computing of one sector, the province's information and communications industry, by 2030, in a plan posted Jul 29, 2026: this section's row of that date); 20 have a plan read that sets none (the 19 of the first count, with Chongqing moved there by a later reading; Zhejiang, moved there by the same reading, now sets a share); 1 is known only from accounts of its plan, the issuer's own news item among them (Tibet, whose 60% is the share of intelligent computing, not of home-made hardware); 1 was not reached (Xinjiang: no regional computing or AI plan text found; the regional pages read set no share). The count is of what was found. The plans of the kind that holds Zhejiang's share (the provincial communications administrations' five-year plans for the information and communications industry) were searched as a class on Nov 25, 2026 for the other 30 units: the plan for 2026 to 2030 was read in full for ten (Beijing, Shanghai, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangxi, Shandong, Henan, Chongqing, Yunnan, Qinghai; Shanghai's and Shandong's in trade sites' copies, their own PDFs being scans) and as a consultation draft for two (Heilongjiang, Guangdong), only the plan for 2021 to 2025 for seven more (Inner Mongolia, Jiangsu, Sichuan, Ningxia, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hainan), and for eleven no plan text was found, only a release or an account (Tianjin, Hebei, Shanxi, Liaoning, Jilin, Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Tibet, Xinjiang). No text read sets a number for a home-made share, so Zhejiang's is the only share found in plans of this kind (this section's entry on the class search; table: tables/provincial_ict_plans.tsv). - **Jan 2025 · Shanghai Commission of Economy and Informatization, guide for building intelligent computing centres, 2025 edition (上海市智算中心建设导则（2025年版）), full text** (a document: the 67-page PDF as Invest Shanghai's site holds it, uploaded Jan 15, 2025 by its address; the commission's own copies answer 404). Organised by the commission and written by the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, it applies in principle to every intelligent computing centre built in the city, for own use or hosted. What it calls the entry requirement (准入要求) for a new centre is energy efficiency (baseline PUE), beside general requirements, among them siting, the operator's licence, rack power, self-assessment and energy use; its post-launch assessment counts load, PUE, water, carbon, green, availability, security and computing grades; it sets no share of home-made chips and no tiers by one: 国产 occurs twice and 自主可控 twice in the whole text, all in two recommendations (宜, should), one for the AI hardware layer and one for edge centres, which are encouraged to use home-made chips. The software layer must support adaptation to several mainstream kinds of AI accelerator. A city bureau dates its release to Jan 10, 2025, and the commission says it set conditions for being allowed to build, assessment standards and procedures. ### 2.4 Regulators' acts against foreign chips

- Market regulator, notice dated Dec 9, 2024 ("发布时间：2024-12-09 19:30" [cn-policy-samr-open-original]), saying it had recently (近日) opened the case: "因英伟达公司涉嫌违反《中华人民共和国反垄断法》... 市场监管总局依法对英伟达公司开展立案调查" (because Nvidia is suspected of violating the Anti-Monopoly Law ... the regulator has, according to law, opened an investigation of Nvidia) [cn-policy-samr-open-original].
- Market regulator, Sept 15, 2025: "经初步调查,英伟达公司违反《中华人民共和国反垄断法》和《市场监管总局关于附加限制性条件批准英伟达公司收购迈络思科技有限公司股权案反垄断审查决定的公告》,市场监管总局依法决定对其实施进一步调查" (a preliminary investigation found that Nvidia violated the Anti-Monopoly Law and the regulator's decision approving its purchase of Mellanox's equity with conditions; the regulator has decided in accordance with the law to investigate further) [cn-policy-samr-further-original].
- Cyberspace regulator, Jul 31, 2025: it "约谈了英伟达公司,要求英伟达公司就对华销售的H20算力芯片漏洞后门安全风险问题进行说明并提交相关证明材料" (summoned Nvidia and required it to explain the security risks of vulnerabilities and backdoors in the H20 chips sold to China and to submit supporting material) [cn-policy-cac-h20-original].
- The precedent: the Cybersecurity Review Office on Micron, published on the cyberspace regulator's site on May 21, 2023 (the office sits in that regulator: "网络安全审查办公室设在国家互联网信息办公室" [cn-policy-review-measures]; corrected Nov 23, 2026: this line had named the regulator itself as the issuer): its products "存在较严重网络安全问题隐患,对我国关键信息基础设施供应链造成重大安全风险" (carry fairly serious hidden dangers of cybersecurity problems and pose a major security risk to the supply chain of China's critical information infrastructure) [cn-policy-micron-decision]. Its operative sentence: "我国内关键信息基础设施的运营者应停止采购美光公司产品" (operators of critical information infrastructure in China shall stop buying Micron's products). The page calls it the review office's conclusion that the products do not pass the review: "网络安全审查办公室依法作出不予通过网络安全审查的结论" [cn-policy-micron-decision]. So when the review office barred a foreign chip maker's products for a class of buyers, the conclusion was published. For Nvidia the pages read hold a summons and no decision. That cuts both ways: Beijing can publish a ban and has not; or its method for Nvidia was unpublished guidance, as the two company filings say.
- Customs Law, article 24: "国家限制进出口的货物,没有进出口许可证件的,不予放行" (goods whose import or export the state restricts shall not be released without licence documents); article 28: "进出口货物应当接受海关查验" (import and export goods shall be subject to customs inspection) [cn-policy-customs-law-wayback, a finance-ministry page in an Internet Archive capture of Apr 10, 2026]. Customs may inspect any goods or articles entering or leaving the country and must not release restricted goods that lack a licence. None of China's published lists of restricted or banned imports that could be read names these chips (the licence lists of 2024 to 2026 and the banned-import lists in force, read whole by script: section 8), so the reported customs holds (Tier 2) may rest on the general inspection power, on a temporary decision outside the lists (the Foreign Trade Law, below) that was not found published, or on something else unpublished.

### 2.6 Published commentary in state and Party media, and an industry body's call

(Tier 1 as published commentary. None of these is an order; they warn, urge or advise. A list of 297 items in central state and Party media on Nvidia and its chips, Jul 2025 to Nov 2026, is tables/state_media_items.tsv (rows 1 to 41 a census of Nov 23, 2026; rows 42 to 74 added from searches and links of Nov 24, 2026; rows 75 to 297 added on Nov 26, 2026 from every saved page of these outlets that names Nvidia or its chips, each coded by the table's rule five times independently, a majority deciding, with thirteen further pages that two more readers found to be second copies of twelve of those items on another site named in column 10 of their item's row; a row of the first census, a notice of Apr 24, 2026 whose page does not name Nvidia, was taken out that day. The table holds what the searches and the saved pages hold: 185 of its items are dated after Sept 24, 2025, far more than before, and it is still a sample of what these outlets printed, not a full count. Its column 13 gives each item's subject: 219 are about the chips for AI computing, 40 about a product with an Nvidia chip, such as a car or a robot, 8 about Nvidia as a company and 30 about another matter that names Nvidia in passing): in the 297 items found, 34 only warn (33 of them about the chips for AI computing and one, a forum report of Sept 24, 2025, about another matter; two of the census's first seven do not speak of buying, and the three census rows added to them, 9, 10 and 11, carry the regulator's notice or demand and speak of the sales to China, not of buying), 23 of them dated Jul 31 to Sept 24, 2025; one a week before, China Daily's excerpt of an outside writer's post, Jul 24, 2025; and ten after: a China Daily report of Nov 1, 2025; six from Dec 9, 2025 to Jan 14, 2026, reports on the American easing for the H200 (China National Radio, Dec 9; Global Times, Dec 11, Dec 16, Jan 6 and Jan 14; Beijing Daily's client, from CCTV, Jan 14); and three in Global Times later in 2026: an industry analyst's words in news reports of Mar 3 and Mar 18, and the paper's own unsigned commentary of Nov 6; 14 mix a warning with a welcome, ten of them after September 2025; 28 welcome Nvidia or its sales in China (among them rows 6, 8, 35, 58 and 66 of the table; two of those five are quoted in section 5); the rest are neutral (126), about self-reliance (74) or other (21). Say «in the 297 items found», never a universal. A baseline for January 2024 to June 2025, gathered by other routes and not a census, is kept apart (tables/state_media_baseline_2024_2025h1.tsv): 174 items since Nov 26, 2026 (49 until then; 125 added the same day from the saved pages, coded the same way, three more pages that proved to be second copies being named in their items' rows), 160 of them in outlets this list covers (the other 14 are in People's Daily group papers it never holds: Securities Times, People's Tribune, China City News); one only warns (a column credited to People's Posts and Telecommunications News, carried on the site of Outlook Weekly, Mar 13, 2025, against relying on the H20), none mixes a warning with a welcome, 15 welcome. With it, 35 items that only warn were found from January 2024 to November 2026: 23 dated Jul 31 to Sept 24, 2025, two before and ten after.)

- **Dec 3, 2024 · Internet Society of China, statement on its own site** (an industry body's published call). It urges Chinese companies to be prudent in buying American chips, to widen cooperation with chip firms of other countries, and to use chips made in China by domestic and foreign-funded firms alike; its stated ground is US export controls, which it says have shaken trust in American chips. Words: "审慎选择采购美国芯片，寻求扩大与其他国家和地区芯片企业的合作，并积极使用内外资企业在华生产制造的芯片" [cn-against2-isc-supply-risk-20241203] (be prudent in choosing to buy American chips, seek wider cooperation with chip firms of other countries and regions, and actively use chips made in China by domestic and foreign-funded firms); "已经动摇业界对美国芯片产品的信任和信心" [cn-against2-isc-supply-risk-20241203]; "2024年12月03日" [cn-against2-isc-supply-risk-20241203]. It is a call for prudence, not abstention, and does not name Nvidia. Cuts: FOR, with that limit.
- **Aug 1, 2025 · People's Daily commentary account, signed commentary by Meng Fanzhe, as carried by Beijing Daily's client (labelled 人民日报评论)** (published commentary). After the cyberspace regulator's summons, it says that to keep cyberspace safe «sick» chips must never be put on duty. [cn-acts-peoplesdaily-bjd-20250801]. Words: "2026-10-28 发布 2026-11-28 实施" [cn-ga31-evallists-49]; "a） 应基于符合安全可靠测评要求的中央处理器（CPU）构建智能云平台。" [cn-ga31-evallists-49]; "应兼容至少一款符合安全可靠测评要求的人工智能训练推理芯片。" [cn-ga31-evallists-49]; "本文件起草单位：中国信息通信研究院、中国航空结算有限责任公司、中国铁塔股份有限公司" [cn-ga31-evallists-49]. A voluntary group standard; «compatible with» one evaluated chip, not built only on such chips. Cuts: FOR, weakly (the evaluation appears in an industry grading).
- **Jul 19, 2025 and Jun 1, 2026 · CGTN and People's Daily welcome Nvidia's return and cooperation** (published commentary; rows of tables/state_media_items.tsv, int16_d r-053 and r-060). CGTN, Jul 19, 2025, «Why must global chip chain stay interconnected?»: "With Nvidia's H20 AI chip returning to the Chinese market – followed closely by AMD's MI308 and easing U.S. restrictions – the message is clear: in an industry defined by precision, complexity and global collaboration, China remains indispensable." [cn-ga31-smcctv-13]. People's Daily, Jun 1, 2026, page 3, 钟声, «推动人工智能成为中美合作的新疆域»: "联想集团与英伟达联合推出“人工智能云超级工厂”，共同布局新一代智能基础设施，为产业升级赋能增效。" [cn-ga31-smpeoples-2] (Lenovo and Nvidia's joint AI cloud «super factory»), among cases of US firms working with China's AI ecosystem, beside its charge that "美方一些人以零和博弈心态看待人工智能，将人工智能技术政治化、工具化、武器化" [cn-ga31-smpeoples-2] (some in the US treat AI as a zero-sum game and politicise and weaponise it) with chip export controls among their measures. Cuts: AGAINST (the welcoming side in Party and state media, in July 2025 and again in June 2026; limit 1).
- **Mar 17, 2025 · China Newsweek (中国新闻周刊), cover story "地方政府，急了", citing a written piece by Shi Chen (史晨), associate researcher at CCID (the industry ministry's research institute, 工业和信息化部赛迪研究院)** (a researcher's written view relayed by the magazine). He wrote that some of the computing built in the last round of computing centres, government purchases to back home-made substitution above all, sits idle: "此前一轮建设的大量智算中心项目，特别是为了扶持国产替代的政府采购，有些算力在闲置" [cn-ga31-smcctv-159]; the magazine's account of his reason: because key parts of the CUDA ecosystem are not open source, running a given model on home-made boards needs heavy adapting, "为什么很多智算中心的算力被闲置，关键就在这里" [cn-ga31-smcctv-159] (that is the key to why computing capacity at many centres sits idle), and the government as buyer "其实有时并不太了解最终用户的需求" [cn-ga31-smcctv-159] (sometimes does not really know what end users need). Cuts: FOR (state purchases backed home-made chips; Shi links idle capacity to the work of adapting home-made boards to run particular models).
- **Jan to Sept 2026, and two pages without publication dates · A common software layer for home-made chips: Beijing's FlagOS, the Internet Society of China's plan to spread it, Shanghai AI Laboratory's test platform, and China Electronics News on the cost of leaving CUDA** (a city government's portal carrying its science commission's report, Jan 7, 2026; an industry body's own account of its Jul 2026 conference; a laboratory's own page, undated; and China Electronics News, Sept 3, 2026, as the trade site 与非网 carries it). On the Beijing government's portal, from the city's science commission and the Zhongguancun administration: the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence released FlagOS 1.6 on Jan 5, and its operator generator KernelGen "已支持英伟达、摩尔线程、华为、海光、天数等多种芯片，可实现跨芯片生成与多端验证，显著降低算子适配与优化成本" [cn-ga31-leadersprovincesp3-40] (supports Nvidia, Moore Threads, Huawei, Hygon, Iluvatar and other chips ... markedly lowering the cost of adapting and tuning operators). The Internet Society of China, at its China Internet Conference of Jul 8 to 10, 2026, launched with the Beijing academy a plan to spread FlagOS, with the China Association of Communication Enterprises, the three telecom carriers and CAICT among its co-founders; it gives the reason as chips that do not work together, "各芯片架构的编程模型、算子体系、通信协议互不兼容" [cn-ga31-associationsp2-16] (the programming models, operator systems and communication protocols of the chip architectures are mutually incompatible), and the reach, "目前该系统已完成18家厂商、32款主流芯片的全场景适配" [cn-ga31-associationsp2-16] (also the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence's community site (智源社区), undated: "成功适配并完成了天数智芯、沐曦、寒武纪、海光、摩尔线程、昆仑芯等六款芯片的端到端训练验证" [cn-ga31-papersacademic-205] (end-to-end training validated on six home-made chips) and "与英伟达基线训练的评测偏差均控制在2%以内" [cn-ga31-papersacademic-205] (results within 2% of an Nvidia baseline, on a 0.6-billion-parameter Qwen model): the Beijing academy's own claim) (adapted to 32 mainstream chips of 18 makers). Shanghai AI Laboratory, setting up a test platform for home-made hardware and software: "当前国内主流验证平台大多依托CUDA生态搭建，适配体系相对单一，对多元国产自研芯片的兼容与支撑能力不足。" [cn-ga31-unilabsp3-38] (the main test platforms in China are mostly built on the CUDA ecosystem and support the many home-made chips poorly; the page gives a working meeting of May 14 and no year). China Electronics News, in its own words: "国产GPU长期面临一个尴尬：芯片单价虽低，但代码迁移、算子补全、性能调优等隐性投入高昂，导致综合使用成本高于国外方案。" [cn-ga31-smsecurities-42] (home-made GPUs have long faced an awkward fact: the chip is cheaper, but the hidden outlay on moving code, filling in operators and tuning is high, so the total cost of use is above the foreign option). The paper also reports that MetaX's MXMACA stack "已支持超过6000个CUDA应用" [cn-ga31-smsecurities-42] (already supports more than 6,000 CUDA applications). Cuts: FOR (Shanghai AI Laboratory says most mainstream Chinese verification platforms rely on CUDA and give limited support to home-made chips, and is working with partners on a platform for domestic hardware and software; China Electronics News says hidden costs have made home-made GPUs costlier to use overall than foreign alternatives), AGAINST in part (the Beijing report credits KernelGen with lowering operator adaptation and tuning costs, and China Electronics News describes MetaX's efforts to lower migration costs).
- **Jun 20, 2025 and Apr 17, 2026 · Reports in Economic Information Daily and on Xinhua's app about Huawei's chips and clusters: a single chip that trails, clusters to make up for it, and an ecosystem that still falls short** (published state-media reports in their own words, with a Huawei official the paper does not name: Economic Information Daily, "华为以集群优势助推算力破局", its address dated Jun 20, 2025; and Xinhua's client, "湖北移动算力版图再扩容", reporter 王政, its address dated Apr 17, 2026). The Huawei official, to Economic Information Daily: "在单芯片相对落后的情况下，华为用数学补物理、非摩尔补摩尔，用集群计算补单芯片" [cn-ga31-smxinhua-70] (with its single chip relatively behind, Huawei makes up with mathematics for physics ... and with cluster computing for the single chip), and of moving users, "帮助他们一天内迁移到昇腾生态上" [cn-ga31-smxinhua-70] (helping them move to the Ascend ecosystem within a day: Huawei's claim); the paper, in its own voice: "相比行业先进，昇腾AI芯片的生态建设仍存一定短板，不少用户需要投入大量精力进行开发和维护" [cn-ga31-smxinhua-70] (compared with advanced ecosystems in the industry, the Ascend chips' ecosystem still falls short in places, and many users must put great effort into development and maintenance). Xinhua, of China Mobile's Ascend 910C cluster in Wuhan: "以384张显卡的集群能力对标H200的单卡优势，有效弥补单芯片性能差距" [cn-ga31-ictpbp3-30] (setting the cluster of 384 cards against the H200's single-card edge, making up the gap in single-chip performance). Cuts: FOR (an unnamed Huawei official said Huawei's single chip was relatively behind, Xinhua described the H200's single-card advantage in its comparison with Wuhan's Ascend 910C cluster, and Economic Information Daily reported that many Ascend users must put substantial effort into development and maintenance), AGAINST in part (Huawei's official described migration tools, and the report on Xinhua's app said the Wuhan cluster made up for a single-chip performance gap).
- **Oct 30, 2026 · People's Daily Online, "坚持AI自主可控与开放合作并举", by a senior economist and a grade-three researcher at the Beijing Academy of Science and Technology** (published commentary; the authors are "北京市科学技术研究院高级经济师、三级研究员" [cn-ga31-smpeoples-43]). It puts Huawei's first-half 2026 AI accelerator shipments at 572,000 (see the IDC count held from Reuters) and calls for faster domestic substitution of high-end training chips: "高端训练芯片的国产替代进程仍需加速，底层框架和原创性算法上的差距并未消失" [cn-ga31-smpeoples-43] (home-made substitution of high-end training chips still needs to speed up; the gap in base frameworks and original algorithms has not gone), while its title asks for self-reliance and open cooperation together. Cuts: FOR on direction, and FOR in part (the commentary calls for faster domestic substitution of high-end training chips), CONTEXT (open cooperation urged beside it).
- **Jul 23, 2026 · Qiushi's site (求是网), signed article "加快发展Token经济，构筑智能时代竞争优势", by a researcher of China Telecom's Party school and an associate professor of Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications** (newspaper commentary carried on the Party journal's site: "作者甘继磊系中国电信党校研究员，张斌系北京邮电大学经济管理学院副教授" [cn-ga31-smdailies-23]). Among the weak points of China's token economy it names dependence abroad, "高端训练与推理AI芯片、集群无损组网技术、高吞吐低延迟推理加速框架等仍较大程度依赖国外产品与生态" [cn-ga31-smdailies-23] (high-end AI chips for training and inference, lossless cluster networking and fast inference frameworks still depend to a large degree on foreign products and ecosystems). The authors also write: "国产算力产品在算子库完备性、分布式并行策略、显存优化等方面与英伟达CUDA生态尚有差距，导致同等功耗下单位Token的生成成本偏高、有效算力转化率偏低" [cn-ga31-smdailies-23] (home-made computing still trails Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem in operator libraries, distributed parallelism and memory optimisation, so the cost of each token is higher at the same power and the useful share of computing lower). Cuts: FOR (on the Party journal's site, the authors link gaps with Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem to higher per-token generation costs and less effective use of compute at the same power draw).
- **Nov 2, 2026 (date in the URL) · China Development Bank's Anhui branch and the Feixing No. 1 cluster, as reported on the Wuhan local financial regulator's site** (a report on a policy bank's lending). The notice uses the words "安全可靠" (compare point 2, tables/chip_evaluations.tsv). Cuts: FOR on direction (encouragement, 鼓励, not a requirement).

## 3. Official and filed documents on what the companies used and wanted

- **Shanghai Municipal Commission of Economy and Informatization**, written reply to proposal No. 0093 of the city's political consultative conference, from its members Fang Qizhong and Zhu Minghua ("方奇钟、朱明华委员" [cn-counter-b11-5]), dated Apr 30, 2025 at its foot ("上海市经济和信息化委员会 2025年4月30日") and published on the commission's site on Nov 10, 2025 ("发布日期:2025-11-10"). (Note, Nov 23, 2026: for about two hours this line said the reply was undated. That was an error: the date stands in the saved page's body and not in its text extract, which was all that had been searched.): "互联网企业自建算力集群,满足市场化企业需求,主要以英伟达高性能卡为主;三大运营商主要购置华为等国产化智算集群" (internet companies build their own computing clusters to meet the needs of market-oriented enterprises, mainly with Nvidia high-performance cards; the three telecom operators mainly buy Huawei and other home-made intelligent-computing clusters) [cn-counter-b11-5]. The passage is about Shanghai's computing suppliers: "从算力供应商来看 , 主要集中在三大电信运营商、上海仪电，以及商汤、腾讯、 阿里、火山等互联网企业" [cn-counter-b11-5], and the operators' purchases are to "提升本市智算多样性" [cn-counter-b11-5] (raise the diversity of the city's intelligent computing). This is a Chinese government body describing, for its own city, the split the position rests on: internet companies mainly on Nvidia cards, the three big operators mainly buying home-made hardware. The operators' own national tenders point the same way (section 3.6).
- **Qiushi and CCID investigation**, carried by the National Data Administration, May 3, 2026: "数百万开发者深度绑定CUDA生态,迁移成本高昂、适配周期漫长,国产替代即便性能达标,规模化应用仍面临障碍" (millions of developers are deeply tied to the CUDA ecosystem; migration is costly and adaptation slow; even where home-made substitutes meet the performance mark, use at scale faces obstacles) [cn-policy-qiushi-cuda-gap].
- **A company's question to the commerce ministry**, on the ministry's public message board, left on Jul 30, 2026 ("留言时间: 2026-07-30") and answered on Aug 19, 2026 (corrected Nov 23, 2026: this file had given the reply's date as the question's; the reply, signed by the ministry's security and control bureau, speaks only of exporters, who must apply for a licence where an item is found to be controlled, "物项确定属于管制范围的，出口经营者应当向国务院商务主管部门申请许可", and does not address imports): "我司计划合规进口H200数据中心GPU,本次咨询该类高端算力芯片的进口合规政策与申报流程" (our company plans to import H200 data-centre GPUs in compliance, and asks about the import compliance policy and declaration procedure for such high-end computing chips) [cn-acts-mofcom-inquiry-20260819].
- **Zhipu, results announcement to the Hong Kong exchange**, Mar 31, 2026: "Faced with the computing power shortage that has outstripped supply since February 2026, we will continue to increase our investments, particularly in the “Day 0” adaptation of domestic chips" [cn-le29-zhipu-results-20260331-en] (a byte-identical copy from Zhipu's investor site, by a sha256 check).
- **Capitalonline (a listed Chinese cloud company), investor-meeting record filed with the exchange**, Feb 17, 2025, asked where it finds the gap between home-made chips and Nvidia's in use: "英伟达芯片通用性强,能在多种 AI 场景 稳定高效运行。国产芯片在通用性上面临一定挑战" (Nvidia chips are highly general-purpose and run stably and efficiently in many AI settings; home-made chips face some challenge in generality); "英伟达的芯片生产规模大,采购成本相对较低, 而国产芯片的生产规模较小,因此采购成本较高" (Nvidia's chips are made at large scale and cost less to buy, while home-made chips are made at smaller scale and cost more) [cn-policy-capitalonline-chip-use]. The company side of the conflict in a filed document; it mentions no state instruction.
- **Nvidia, Form 10-Q** (quarter to Jul 28, 2024), fifteen months before the reported purchase guidance: "an agency of the Chinese government announced an Action Plan that endorses new standards regarding the compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth of accelerators used in new and renovated data centers in China."; "If the Chinese government modifies or implements the Action Plan in a way that effectively prevents us from being able to design products to meet the new standard, this may restrict the ability of customers to use some of our data center products" [cn-policy-nvidia-plan-2024]. Which agency and plan it means is not established: the plan is not among the saved pages.
- **Against a simple conflict: the companies' own chips.** Baidu, Form 20-F for 2024: "Baidu AI chips have been used for our search engine, cloud, and Xiaodu’s business needs, while powering our deep learning computing needs." [cn-policy-baidu-own-chip-wayback, an Internet Archive capture of May 27, 2025]. Alibaba, results release of Mar 19, 2026: "chip design subsidiary T-Head has brought proprietary GPUs into scaled production." [cn-policy-alibaba-own-gpu]. Two of the companies named as wanting Nvidia chips tell investors they have programmes of their own; neither says what share of its computing those chips carry. Baidu's report ties its chip-supply risk to US export controls, not to Chinese pressure: "如果我們因出口管制而無法採購足夠數量的先進半導體芯片，我們可能面臨重大挑戰，包括產能受限、成本上升及效能下降。" [cn-le07-baidu-2025-hkar].
- **Results calls (added Nov 23, 2026; quotations checked by script).** Nvidia, May 20, 2026: "While the US government has approved licenses for H200 to be shipped to China-based customers, we have yet to generate any revenue, and we are uncertain whether any imports will be allowed into the country." [cn-o38-nvda-q1fy27-call-transcript-pdf]. Nvidia, call for the quarter ended Oct 25, 2026: "Q3 sales of licensed Hopper Data Center products to China was $2.4 billion. Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper Data Center products included, and we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper Data Center products to China." [cn-o38-nvda-q3fy27-call-transcript-pdf]; no reason is given. Tencent's chief strategy officer, May 13, 2026 (as a stock-data site's transcript and Sina Tech's Chinese record [cn-ga31-tencentcall-1] label the speaker; a Chinese transcript on Xueqiu labels the same answer the chief financial officer's [cn-ga31-tencentcall-25]; Tencent's replay was not reachable): "a combination of policy restrictions on certain, you know, foreign design GPUs being brought into China. The China design GPUs, you know, facing limited fab capacity within China." [cn-o36-tencent-call-20260513-sa]; he does not say whose policy. The same officer, Mar 18, 2026: "higher-end imported GPUs which are now becoming available again" [cn-o36-tencent-call-20260318-sa]. Across 39 saved calls of Alibaba, Tencent and Baidu (Nov 2023 to Nov 2026) a reading of them found no executive naming Nvidia or a Chinese order: `outputs/A11_records/idea36_results_calls/results_calls.md`; across 61 calls of 8 companies (Jan 2025 to Nov 2026) a separate search found nobody saying Nvidia or Huawei, with a control (section 3.5 and section 8). The same Tencent officer on May 13, 2026 went on: "we haven't faced those sort of artificial additional constraints on CPU or networking chips" [cn-o36-tencent-call-20260513-sa].
- **Alibaba, annual report to the SEC** (year to Mar 31, 2026): "In September 2025, the Cyberspace Administration of China requested Chinese technology companies to halt purchases of certain chips." [cn-clips-alibaba-20f]
- **Nvidia, Form 10-Q** (quarter to Jul 26, 2026): the US "granted licenses that would allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers, but such sales were restricted by the PRC government" [man-ms-sec-10q-2026-07].
- **Nvidia's own revenue from customers headquartered in China and Hong Kong, by quarter (added Nov 23, 2026; each figure read in a filing's own table or, where marked, got by subtraction of two such figures, in millions of dollars).** Quarter ended Oct 27, 2024: 8,142. Jan 26, 2025: 7,818 (by subtraction: 25,048 for the fiscal year less 17,230 for its first nine months). Apr 27, 2025: 9,659. Jul 27, 2025: 3,985. Oct 26, 2025: 2,973. Jan 25, 2026: 3,060 (by subtraction: 19,677 for the fiscal year less 16,617 for its first nine months). Apr 26, 2026: 4,550. Jul 26, 2026: 7,880. Oct 25, 2026: 11,050, of total revenue of 115,844. Sources: the quarterly report signed Nov 19, 2025 [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-10], the annual report for the year ended Jan 25, 2026 [man-ms-sec-10k-fy2026], the quarterly reports for the quarters ended Apr 26 and Jul 26, 2026 [man-ms-sec-10q-2026-04] [man-ms-sec-10q-2026-07], and the Form 8-K of Nov 17, 2026 [ms-p3-nvda-8k-20261117-pdf]. So the line fell by about two thirds between spring and autumn 2025 and then rose to its highest value of the nine quarters in the quarter ended Oct 25, 2026. All nine are on the headquarters basis Nvidia adopted in its 10-Q of Nov 19, 2025, with earlier periods recast; the filings before that counted by billing location, as that 10-Q says ("Previously, revenue by geographic area was reported based on the billing location of our customers" [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-10]), and the one earlier filing read here printed a lower figure for its quarter (5,416 for the quarter ended Oct 27, 2024) [man-ms-nvda-2024q3-10q-58a58e]. **What it does not show:** chips entering China. Nvidia's note on the table: "Revenue by geographic region is designated based on the location of the headquarters of direct customers. The end customer and shipping location may be different from our direct customers' headquarters location." [ms-p3-nvda-8k-20261117-pdf] The line covers every product, not only AI chips, and the same filing lists equipment makers and distributors among direct customers, "such as add-in board manufacturers, or AIBs, distributors, original design manufacturers, or ODMs, original equipment manufacturers, or OEMs" [ms-p3-nvda-8k-20261117-pdf]. Of the latest quarter Nvidia said that "Q3 sales of licensed Hopper Data Center products to China was $2.4 billion" [cn-o38-nvda-q3fy27-call-transcript-pdf]. Not yet used in the argument.

- **The two approvals, and the foreclosure put on US controls (Nov 19, 2025 onward).** From the 10-Q for the quarter to Oct 26, 2025 Nvidia says it cannot make a competitive product for China's data-centre market that both governments approve (its 10-Q for the quarter to Jul 27, 2025, signed Aug 27, 2025, named only the USG), and in the same filings it says it is already effectively foreclosed from the China market by US export controls. Words: "Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China's data center market that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government." [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-10]; the 10-Q for the quarter to Jul 27, 2025, before: "We may be unable to create a competitive product for China's data center market that receives approval from the USG." [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-07]; "Although we are already effectively foreclosed from the China market by U.S. export controls" [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-10]; the annual report: "As of the end of fiscal year 2026, we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market" [man-ms-sec-10k-fy2026]. Cuts: FOR (Beijing named as a second approver) and AGAINST (the foreclosure is put down to US controls) at once.
- **The H20 and H200 licences: «restricted by the PRC government» first in the 10-Q of Aug 26, 2026.** Earlier filings give amounts and no cause; the 10-Q for the quarter to Jul 26, 2026 says both chips' licensed sales were restricted by the PRC government, and the H200 charge follows that sentence directly. Words: Nov 2025, "but to date, we have generated approximately $50 million in H20 revenue under those licenses" [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-10]; Feb 2026, "We generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under those licenses." [man-ms-sec-10k-fy2026] and "To date, we have not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program, and do not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China." [man-ms-sec-10k-fy2026]; Aug 2026, "Beginning in August 2025, the USG granted licenses that would have allowed us to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers, but such sales were restricted by the PRC government, and we were unable to sell our H20 inventory." [man-ms-sec-10q-2026-07]; "The U.S. government, or USG, granted licenses that would allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers, but such sales were restricted by the PRC government, and we have been unable to sell all the products for which we have licenses." [man-ms-sec-10q-2026-07]; next: "During the first half of fiscal year 2027, we incurred a $0.4 billion charge associated with H200 for excess inventory and purchase obligations, as the demand for H200 products diminished." [man-ms-sec-10q-2026-07]; and "After incurring that charge, we have made a fraction of the allowed shipments under the USG's H200 licensing program. Those shipments account for less than 1% of Data Center revenue in our most recent quarter." [man-ms-sec-10q-2026-07]. Revenue under a licence is a sale to a China-based customer; it does not say where the chips went. Cuts: FOR.
- **American conditions on the H200, in the same filings.** The licences require inspection in the United States, a 25% tariff applies on import into the United States for that inspection, and Nvidia could not pass any of it on. Words: "The license requires that the H200s go through an inspection process in the United States prior to any shipment to the customer." [man-ms-sec-10k-fy2026]; "any H200 shipped under the new licensing program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States." [man-ms-sec-10k-fy2026]; "We have been unable to pass along any of the tariff to our customers, and do not anticipate doing so in the event we are able to sell licensed products into the China market." [man-ms-sec-10q-2026-07]; and of the H20: "USG officials have expressed an expectation that the USG will receive 15% of the revenue generated from licensed H20 sales, but to date, the USG has not published a regulation codifying such requirement." [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-07]. Cuts: AGAINST «only Beijing stood in the H200's way».
- **The H20 under the April 2025 US licence rule.** Words: "Sales of our H20 products were $4.6 billion for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 prior to the new export licensing requirements." [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-04]; "As a result of these new requirements, we incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations as the demand for H20 products diminished." [man-ms-sec-10q-2025-04]; the commentary on that quarter: "This outlook reflects a loss in H20 revenue of approximately $8.0 billion due to the recent export control limitations." [cn-le05-q1fy26-cfo-commentary]. Cuts: CONTEXT (limit 4: American curbs).
- **The antitrust finding, in Nvidia's words.** From Nov 2025 the filings say China's antitrust regulators found on Sept 15, 2025 that Nvidia's compliance with US export controls, which made it offer degraded products to China, discriminated unfairly against Chinese customers. Regulators had "inquired" from the 10-Q of Nov 2023. The report names no chip. Cuts: CONTEXT (Moonshot AI used a provincial computing voucher; what chips the computing ran on is not said).
